findings.title: The specified send call throws before a byte leaves, and the line is forbidden by the structural assertion the egress guarantee rests on
findings.problem: §2.5 step 7 is net.request(url, { method:'POST', body: gate.body, ... }). (a) `net` is electron/lib/http.cjs (modelRouter.cjs:11) whose request() does Buffer.byteLength(body) at L112 and req.write(body) at L141 — body must be a STRING, while gate.body is an object (§12(g) asserts it carries model, stream:false and a messages array). Buffer.byteLength({}) throws TypeError, request() catches it, burns both retries and returns { ok:false, status:0 }, which §8 row 14 reads as offline:true — so the feature reports the network as down on a working machine. (b) §12(g) asserts 'ollamaCloud.cjs source contains no JSON.stringify and no `body:` assignment'; §2.5 step 7 IS a `body:` assignment in that file, so the suite fails on the specified line and the cheap resolution is to delete the only assertion standing between this design and a second body constructor.
findings.fix: Use net.post(`${base}/api/chat`, gate.body, { headers: authHeader(), timeout, retries: 1 }) and net.get(`${base}/api/tags`, { headers: authHeader(), timeout: 15000, retries: 1 }). http.cjs post() (L177-186) stringifies a non-string body INSIDE http.cjs and spreads opts.headers over Content-Type, so Authorization passes and ollamaCloud.cjs contains no JSON.stringify and no `body:` key. Restate §12(g): 'ollamaCloud.cjs contains no JSON.stringify, no `body:` key and no call to net.request; the only outbound calls are net.post/net.get passing assemble's body by reference; egressBoundary.cjs requires no http client.' Add to §12(h) a positive assertion that the dummy-key success path returns ok:true with content — a throw inside request() currently satisfies every existing §12(h) assertion.

findings.title: I-SECRETS-planted-md has no file to plant into, so npm run audit and verify:covenant go red on the first commit
findings.problem: Measured this session: zero .md files exist under electron/, src/, server/, shared/ or scripts/. The census over §12.2(b)'s exact file set is 194 files (confirming §1.12 fact 7 precisely): .cjs 103, .jsx 43, .js 36, .mjs 9, .json 3, .md 0. So §12.2(c)'s pick returns undefined and selfTest() hits 'if (!rel) { r.fail(`${m.id}: no file to mutate`); continue; }' (verifyInvariants.cjs L1050-1052) — the SELF row goes red and both npm run audit and npm run verify:covenant fail immediately, which is the same 'red on the first commit so the check gets disabled' failure §12.2(b) exists to avoid. Adding a .md file would not help: selfTest builds everyFile from INVARIANTS.flatMap(i=>i.files) + walkShipped(ROOT) + three literals, and walkShipped's extension set is {.cjs,.mjs,.js,.jsx} (L217), so copyInto skips the .md and fs.readFileSync(target) at L1056 throws ENOENT OUTSIDE runRowSilently, crashing the harness. Related: with 0 .md and 3 .json (all in shared/, two of them protected) inside the five trees, the .md half of walkForSecrets scans nothing.
findings.fix: Preferred: assert the per-extension view choice in scannerSelfCheck() (verifyInvariants.cjs:244), which already exists to prove the scanner on synthetic strings and needs no file on disk — three checks: a .md body scanned raw keeps the line after a // in a URL; a .cjs string literal survives the nc view; a .cjs comment does not. Then MUTATIONS gains exactly one case (I-SECRETS-planted, targeting electron/**/*.cjs, which walkShipped does copy) and §14 says fourteen cases, not fifteen. Alternative: target shared/resourceCatalog.json (the only non-protected .json in the trees), rename the case I-SECRETS-planted-json, and add that path to the I-SECRETS row's `files` array — INVARIANTS.flatMap(i=>i.files) is the only route by which a non-walkShipped extension reaches the sandbox. Either way state in §12.2(b) that .md matches zero files inside the five trees and that docs/ is covered by §12.3's prefix sweep alone.

findings.title: The only renderer caller drops every field that makes absence honest and the path visible
findings.problem: ramaClient.js L19-37 (verified) forwards only { ok, sessionId, message, model, fallbackFrom, usage } on success and returns { ok:false, error: res?.error || 'Model router returned no content' } on failure. So unconfigured, remedy, failures, gateError, path, endpoint, via and credentialSource never reach a renderer. Against the brief: the absent-key state is reported ABSENT/UNCONFIGURED by the IPC response and as a bare error to master, with the one actionable sentence (remedy) deleted one function above him — §3.4(b) replaced 'All models failed' with text nobody receives; and 'which path served a request must be visible' is false, since path/endpoint/via/credentialSource are built, asserted in §12(e), then discarded. §3.4(b)'s 'the substitution and its cause are both declared' also fails: fallbackFrom survives, unconfigured does not. §12(g3) asserts only that the call object includes `user`, so the suite is green while all of this is true.
findings.fix: Specify the forwarding and widen §14's row from 2 lines to ~10. Success: add unconfigured, path, endpoint, via, credentialSource (each ?? null) beside model/fallbackFrom/usage. Failure: return { ok:false, error, unconfigured: res?.unconfigured ?? null, failures: res?.failures ?? null, remedy: res?.remedy ?? null, gateError: res?.gateError ?? false }. Add to §12(g3): a structural assertion that ramaClient.js's FAILURE return includes remedy and unconfigured and its SUCCESS return includes path. And name in §14 the one surface that renders it — src/pages/Chat/Chat.jsx's res.ok === false branch appends res.remedy when present — otherwise the forwarding stops one layer higher and the finding re-opens there.

findings.title: --diagnose's specified probe cannot be awaited: diagnose() is synchronous and probeLocal does not exist
findings.problem: §7.3 specifies `const daemonUp = await probeLocal('127.0.0.1', 11434, 500);` inside diagnose(). Verified: start.cjs:318 is `function diagnose() {` — not async — so `await` there is a SyntaxError that `node --check start.cjs` catches, failing the project's own verification bar. diagnose() has two un-awaited call sites, start.cjs:1474 (destructuring `{ defects, report, degraded }`) and start.cjs:1514; both are inside async main() so they CAN be awaited, but making diagnose() async changes its return type and breaks both destructures until changed, and §14 mentions neither. probeLocal does not exist anywhere in the tree and has no specified signature, return type or failure behaviour. The .env warning in the same section is fine — fs.readFileSync is synchronous and is the part carrying the security value.
findings.fix: Preferred: drop the probe from diagnose(). Keep it synchronous, keep the two add() lines that need no I/O plus the .env warning, delete the `if (!daemonUp)` block, and let models:cloud-status (§7.1) own daemon reachability since it can read the vault and can be async. Alternative: state that diagnose() becomes `async function diagnose()`, that BOTH start.cjs:1474 and start.cjs:1514 become `await diagnose()`, list both in §14, and specify probeLocal(host, port, ms) -> Promise<boolean> that resolves false on any error or timeout and binds loopback only (http is already required at start.cjs:46, so no new import is needed).

findings.title: §12(e)'s positive reachability assertion has no seam, and the design calls it the proof the feature works at all
findings.problem: §12(e) asserts that with a stub vault holding the dummy key and no daemon, selectModel('general') returns an ollama-cloud/* id — §10 calls this 'the one assertion that proves the feature is reachable on the target machine'. selectModel reaches the vault via checkAvailable -> getCredential, and modelRouter.cjs:10 is `const { getCredential } = require('./credentialVault.cjs')` — a destructured binding captured at load time. All four seams (§2.2's useVault/useStore/useHttp/useOrchestrator) are on ollamaCloud.cjs; none reaches that binding, and patching credentialVault's exports after modelRouter loads has no effect. So the negative half of §12(e) works by accident (a locked real vault returns null) and the positive half is unreachable. Same gap governs §12(d) (models:chat's unconfigured chain), §12(g2)'s positive case through 'the real switch', and §12(j). Also unflagged: §10 says 'no Electron', but modelRouter.cjs -> credentialVault.cjs:13 requires electron at module scope. Survivable (the electron package's main export is a path string, so `app` is undefined and getVaultPath()'s os.homedir() fallback applies) but it means the suite needs node_modules installed and, without a stub, would mkdirSync under master's home directory and open the path of his real vault file.
findings.fix: Specify the seam in §10 and §12(e) as a require-cache stub installed BEFORE modelRouter is loaded: resolve ../electron/ipc/credentialVault.cjs, set require.cache[path] = { id, filename, loaded:true, children:[], exports: { register(){}, isUnlocked: () => vaultUnlocked, getCredential: (s) => (vaultUnlocked && vaultHasKey && s === 'OLLAMA_API_KEY' ? 'test-not-a-real-key' : null), setCredentialDirect(){}, deleteCredentialDirect(){} } }, then require modelRouter. Add to §11.8 that verifyOllamaCloud.cjs requires node_modules because modelRouter reaches electron transitively. Add to §12(j) an assertion that no file or directory under userData/~/.rama-agi is created by the suite.

findings.title: _awaitSlot as specified lets two CRITICAL waiters both take a maxConcurrent:1 row
findings.problem: The spec is `const got = await this._awaitSlot(provider, waitMs); // resolves on 'slot:released'` with releaseSlot emitting an event 'that waiters listen for'. With two CRITICAL requests waiting and one releaseSlot, both listeners fire, both _awaitSlot calls resolve truthy, and both reserveSlot calls return { ok:true } — inFlight reaches 2 on a row whose maxConcurrent is 1, i.e. the exact free-tier limit the brief says must be corrected, broken by the mechanism added to honour it. §6.3 says CRITICAL 'QUEUES at the head' but specifies only an event, no queue and no re-check rule, and §12(i) asserts a single waiter so the suite cannot see it.
findings.fix: Specify a re-check loop with the increment in the same synchronous turn as the test, so exactly one waiter wins per release: look the row up with hasOwnProperty (return false if absent), then `for(;;) { if (limit.inFlight < limit.maxConcurrent) { limit.inFlight++; return true; } const left = deadline - Date.now(); if (left <= 0) return false; await this._onceOrTimeout('slot:released', left); }`. State that reserveSlot does NOT increment again when _awaitSlot returns true, otherwise the fix double-counts. Add to §12(i): two CRITICAL waiters on a held maxConcurrent:1 row then ONE releaseSlot — exactly one resolves { ok:true, waited:true }, the other stays pending, and inFlight === 1.

findings.title: assemble({ kind: 'search' })'s body is never specified, while §5.3 says webSearch uses it verbatim and §12(g) asserts a complete body for chat only
findings.problem: §5.3 says webSearch calls assemble({ kind:'search', query, maxResults }) and 'uses the returned body verbatim', and §12(g)'s positive assertion covers model/stream/messages — i.e. chat only. Nothing says what body contains for a search, and §11.3/§11.12 admit the endpoint path, body and response shape are unknown and 'cannot be implemented from this document alone'. So the one-constructor rule holds in letter while the search body's field names are invented inside assemble, unreviewed — the same outcome §12(g) exists to prevent, moved one function inward. All of §12(g)'s search assertions test refusals, so an invented or empty accepted body passes.
findings.fix: Either pin a placeholder and label it: for kind:'search' return { ok:true, maxLevel, counts:{messages:0,parts:0}, body:{ query: query.text, max_results: clamp(maxResults,1,10) } } with a comment that it is PROVISIONAL on §11.3 and that the only permitted change when the real shape is read is the field names INSIDE assemble — plus a §12(g) assertion that an accepted search body's only caller-derived value is query.text and it carries no key outside { query, max_results }. Or defer webSearch() from this tranche (the credential, the ollama-search row, models:search-web's gate-above-backend-selection, the browserEngine.searchWeb extraction and every refusal assertion still land) and say so in §5.2, §13.2(3) and §14.

findings.title: orchestrator:api-limits ships the whole row, so the new monthly counters become an ungated renderer surface outside §2.2's discipline
findings.where: §6.2's row shape; §6.3's monthly accounting; resourceOrchestrator.cjs's orchestrator:api-limits handler
findings.problem: Verified: `ipcMain.handle('orchestrator:api-limits', async () => ({ ok:true, data: API_RATE_LIMITS }))` — the whole object, no capability check. §6.2 adds maxConcurrent, inFlight, monthlyTokenBudget, usedTokMonth, monthStartedAt and a prose note to the ollama-cloud row and §6.3 persists the monthly counters, all of it then handed to any renderer that asks with no gate and no projection, while getStatus() projects explicitly to { used, cap, pct } — so the two surfaces will disagree about what a rate-limit row is. Not a credential leak (nothing in the row derives from the key) but a new unmentioned renderer surface that contradicts §2.2's rule of one definition with the renderer surface provably narrower, which §12.4(7b) asserts for models:cloud-status. A later session will read this as licence to expose a rate-limit row wholesale.
findings.fix: Add to §6.2: orchestrator:api-limits returns API_RATE_LIMITS wholesale and is ungated; the rows this tranche adds carry no value derived from the credential, so the exposure is acceptable — and the rule is written down so it stays true: NO field may be added to any API_RATE_LIMITS row that derives from a credential value. getStatus().apiLimits keeps its explicit projection and gains inFlight and maxConcurrent; usedTokMonth and monthStartedAt are reported through ollamaCloud.status(), the surface §2.2 freezes. Add to §12(i): no own-property of any row matches /key|secret|bearer|prefix|hash/i, and the §12.4 dummy key does not appear in JSON.stringify(API_RATE_LIMITS) after a full cloud call.

findings.title: The secret matcher's digit discriminator creates a false-negative class and is not needed: !WORDY alone silences both measured false positives
findings.problem: §12.2(b) specifies candidate = s => !WORDY.test(s) && /\d/.test(s) && entropy(s) >= 3.5, and §131.3 and the ledger row both assert that 'without those two discriminators it is measurably red on the first commit'. Measured this session against the two named strings: 'locally-privileged-but-HTTP-reachable' (src/services/ghostMode.js:130) and 'ABSOLUTE_LOYALTY_TO_KRISHNA_PRASAD_SECRET_MATRIX' (scripts/verifySelfModel.cjs:307) are both all-letters-and-separators, so WORDY matches both and the digit test does no work against either. (The ghostMode string is additionally inside a JSDoc block, so the nc view blanks it anyway.) Keeping the digit test therefore buys nothing measured and silently excludes every digit-free credential — not exotic, since any 32+ char alphabetic slice of a longer token is one. The claim is also already written into the ready-to-paste blocks.
findings.fix: Drop the digit requirement, keep !WORDY: `const candidate = s => !WORDY.test(s) && entropy(s) >= 3.5;` with the measurement in a comment (194 files, 0 entropy hits with !WORDY alone; both would-be hits are all-letter runs matching WORDY; a digit test was considered and REJECTED because it adds nothing against either and excludes every digit-free token). If the digit test is kept instead, state in §12.2(b) that a digit-free high-entropy literal is a KNOWN, ACCEPTED miss with the prefix matcher as its only defence. Correct §131.3 and the ledger row either way — both currently assert a measurement that does not hold.

findings.title: _tick's increment is described as 'unguarded' and is not; the real hazard differs and the false sentence is headed for a tracked file
findings.problem: All four call _tick's increment an 'unguarded bracket read'. Verified at resourceOrchestrator.cjs:250 it is `if (task.aiProvider && API_RATE_LIMITS[task.aiProvider]) { API_RATE_LIMITS[task.aiProvider].usedReq++; ... }` — guarded by truthiness, not by ownership. The hazard is real and worse than the phrase conveys: API_RATE_LIMITS['__proto__'] resolves through the prototype chain to Object.prototype, which is TRUTHY, so the guard PASSES and .usedReq++ writes NaN onto Object.prototype — prototype pollution affecting every plain object in the process, from one free-text field in Resources.jsx. The prescribed hasOwnProperty fix is unchanged and correct. It matters because §1.12 is the document's own verification record and §131.7 plus the ledger row are ready-to-paste blocks destined for docs/research/OLLAMA_CLOUD.md — round 2's worst finding was exactly this shape, a false statement about existing code shipping into a tracked file.
findings.fix: Replace the phrase in all four places: '_tick (L250) guards by truthiness, not ownership: API_RATE_LIMITS["__proto__"] resolves through the prototype chain to Object.prototype, which is truthy, so the guard passes and .usedReq++ writes onto Object.prototype — prototype pollution from a free-text UI field. hasOwnProperty closes it, the same guard _canRun, admit and recordApiUse take.' Add to §12(i): after _tick runs with aiProvider '__proto__', Object.prototype.usedReq === undefined — asserted, because the symptom of this bug appears nowhere near its cause.

findings.title: Whether listModels() may mutate MODEL_REGISTRY is unspecified, and the house pattern says yes
findings.problem: §2.6 gives listModels() a return shape and §11.5 names it as the mechanism that will 'reconcile' the thirteen inferred apiModel values, without saying whether reconciliation is report-only or writes the registry. Both sibling Ollama paths in the same file do refresh-and-merge (verified: refreshOllamaModels rebuilds discoveredOllama from the daemon probe; refreshCustomProviders at modelRouter.cjs:86-91 deletes its tracked ids then Object.assigns fresh ones into MODEL_REGISTRY), so an implementer following the house pattern would naturally have models:cloud-list merge discovered rows — at which point rows exist whose daemonTag was never in the frozen table, which §4.2's 'null for anything not in it — never a derived guess' forbids, and §12(f)'s per-row assertions iterate CLOUD_TAGS so they would not see them.
findings.fix: One sentence in §2.6 and one in §14: listModels() is REPORT-ONLY. It never writes MODEL_REGISTRY, never adds a row and never fills a daemonTag the table does not hold — unlike refreshOllamaModels and refreshCustomProviders, which do merge. Reconciling an inferred apiModel is a SOURCE EDIT to CLOUD_TAGS, reviewed and committed, not a runtime mutation: the table is the authority in both directions and a runtime-added row would have no attested daemon tag. Add to §12(f): MODEL_REGISTRY's set of ollama-cloud/* ids is unchanged after a successful listModels() call against the stub.

findings.title: Name the HTTP binding in the new module, because `net` reads as Electron's net
findings.problem: net.request is correct IN modelRouter.cjs, where net is a local alias for lib/http.cjs (modelRouter.cjs:11; browserEngine.cjs:60 uses the same alias). But electron/lib/ollamaCloud.cjs is new, and `net` is also Electron's own HTTP module — whose net.request would be a real I9 breach with no circuit breaker, no 429 backoff and no response cap.
findings.fix: Write the binding in §2.2: `const http = injectedHttp ?? require('./http.cjs');` with a comment that it is named http and not net because Electron's net.request is a different thing and must never be used here. §12.2(a)'s asserted specifier './http.cjs' is right as written.

findings.title: .env.example's HMAC_SECRET placeholder is a credential-adjacent high-entropy literal that only the prefix matcher sees
